dedupe_keys.name: cambridge housing model england housing stock energy model

description: The Cambridge Housing Model couples English Housing Survey 2011 data with a SAP-based energy calculator to estimate energy use and CO2 emissions for all homes in England, broken down by final use. Cambridge Architectural Research developed it to underpin the 2012 Housing Energy Fact File and Energy Consumption in the UK and to inform housing policy; the government published it to encourage scrutiny and transparency and invited feedback. The GOV.UK page was first published on 18 August 2010 and last updated on 22 October 2015, and now sits under the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and the former Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy. Coverage: the English housing stock. Access: the model and a user guide are linked from GOV.UK. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): OGL-UK-3.0 (GOV.UK site-wide statement: all content available under OGL v3.0 except where otherwise stated). Caveats: based on 2011 survey data, and the page says the model was still being developed. Simulation uses: national housing energy baselines and policy scenario checks. Related records: BREDEM and the CREST Demand Model.
